chapter_title: Organic Compounds: Alkanes and Their Stereochemistry

questions.chapter_title: Organic Compounds: Alkanes and Their Stereochemistry
questions.question: What is the expected major product when Propane (C3H8) is treated with 5 equivalents O2 / flame?
questions.explanation: Treating Propane (C3H8) with 5 equivalents O2 / flame yields 3 CO2 + 4 H2O. Rationale: Complete oxidation of alkane hydrocarbons under excess oxygen yields carbon dioxide and water.

questions.chapter_title: Organic Compounds: Alkanes and Their Stereochemistry
questions.question: Which reagent or set of reaction conditions will best accomplish the transformation of Ethane (CH3CH3) into Chloroethane (CH3CH2Cl) + HCl?
questions.explanation: To convert Ethane (CH3CH3) into Chloroethane (CH3CH2Cl) + HCl, the appropriate reagent is Cl2 / hν (light). Rationale: Light initiates homolytic Cl-Cl cleavage, triggering a free-radical chain substitution.

questions.chapter_title: Organic Compounds: Alkanes and Their Stereochemistry
questions.question: What is the expected major product when Propane (CH3CH2CH3) is treated with Br2 / hν (light)?
questions.explanation: Treating Propane (CH3CH2CH3) with Br2 / hν (light) yields 2-Bromopropane (major) + HBr. Rationale: Bromine radical selectively abstracts the weaker secondary C-H bond to generate the more stable 2° radical.

questions.chapter_title: Organic Compounds: Alkanes and Their Stereochemistry
questions.question: Which reagent or set of reaction conditions will best accomplish the transformation of 2-Methylpropane ((CH3)3CH) into 2-Bromo-2-methylpropane (major, >99%) + HBr?
questions.explanation: To convert 2-Methylpropane ((CH3)3CH) into 2-Bromo-2-methylpropane (major, >99%) + HBr, the appropriate reagent is Br2 / hν (light). Rationale: High selectivity of bromine leads almost exclusively to tertiary C-H abstraction forming 3° alkyl bromide.

questions.chapter_title: Organic Compounds: Alkanes and Their Stereochemistry
questions.question: What is the expected major product when Decane (C10H22) is treated with High heat / silica-alumina catalyst?
questions.explanation: Treating Decane (C10H22) with High heat / silica-alumina catalyst yields Pentane (C5H12) + 1-Pentene (C5H10). Rationale: Thermal cracking cleaves C-C bonds homolytically to yield smaller alkane and alkene fuel fragments.

questions.chapter_title: Organic Compounds: Alkanes and Their Stereochemistry
questions.question: Which reagent or set of reaction conditions will best accomplish the transformation of Eclipsed ethane into Staggered ethane (lowest energy)?
questions.explanation: To convert Eclipsed ethane into Staggered ethane (lowest energy), the appropriate reagent is Thermal rotation at 25°C. Rationale: Overcoming the 12 kJ/mol torsional strain barrier yields the stable staggered conformation.

questions.chapter_title: Organic Compounds: Alkanes and Their Stereochemistry
questions.question: Which starting material will react with C2-C3 bond rotation to yield Anti-butane (lowest energy conformer) as the major product?
questions.explanation: Gauche-butane reacts with C2-C3 bond rotation to yield Anti-butane (lowest energy conformer). Rationale: The anti conformation minimizes steric clash between terminal methyl groups at 180° dihedral angle.

questions.chapter_title: Organic Compounds: Alkanes and Their Stereochemistry
questions.question: What is the expected major product when Ethane (CH3CH3) is treated with Pt catalyst / 500°C?
questions.explanation: Treating Ethane (CH3CH3) with Pt catalyst / 500°C yields Ethylene (H2C=CH2) + H2. Rationale: High-temperature catalytic elimination of hydrogen converts saturated alkanes to alkenes.

questions.chapter_title: Organic Compounds: Alkanes and Their Stereochemistry
questions.question: Which starting material will react with Cl2 / light to yield 1-Chloro-2-methylpropane (65%) + 2-Chloro-2-methylpropane (35%) as the major product?
questions.explanation: 2-Methylpropane ((CH3)3CH) reacts with Cl2 / light to yield 1-Chloro-2-methylpropane (65%) + 2-Chloro-2-methylpropane (35%). Rationale: Chlorine's lower selectivity results in substantial primary substitution due to 9 primary vs 1 tertiary hydrogens.

questions.chapter_title: Organic Compounds: Alkanes and Their Stereochemistry
questions.question: What is the expected major product when Hexane (C6H14) is treated with Thermal cracking (700°C)?
questions.explanation: Treating Hexane (C6H14) with Thermal cracking (700°C) yields Ethylene + Propene + Methane mixture. Rationale: High-temperature pyrolysis fragments the carbon skeleton into commercial low-molecular-weight olefins.
